notesStmt.note: Whitman has written the date May 2, 1887, at the top, which is likely the date that the manuscript was composed.

A late draft of "Not Meagre, Latent Boughs Alone," first published in Lippincott's Magazine in November 1887. It appeared, along with three other poems, as part of a cluster titled "November Boughs." It was later included in Whitman's standalone volume of the same name (1888).

lg.l:
Not meager, latent boughs
alone, O songs, (scaly
and bare, like eagles'
talons,)

But haply for some sunny
day, (who knows?)—some
future spring, some
summer—bursting forth.

Blossoms To and verdant
leaves, and ‸sheltering shade, and—to
nourishing fruit,

Apples and grapes—roses
and —the stalwart limbs
of trees ‸emerging——and fresh

And fresh, free, perfumed,
open air,

And love and faith, like
‸scented roses blooming.
